bug_semantics: phpMyFAQ public child-resource APIs (GET /api/v3.1/comments/{recordId} and GET /api/v3.1/attachments/{recordId}) return comments and attachment metadata keyed only by numeric FAQ record ID, without checking whether the current requester can view that parent FAQ. Parent FAQ reads already apply user/group permission, active-flag, and date-window filters: FaqController::getFaq returns 404 when solution_id is the access-denied sentinel 42, while the frontend substitutes Translation msgAccessDenied for the article body. Unauthenticated attackers who enumerate record IDs can still retrieve restricted comment bodies, commenter usernames and email addresses, and attachment filenames. The frontend FAQ page has the same comments gap (Access denied body, comments still rendered). CWE-862. Vendor/CVE range is phpMyFAQ before 4.1.7; 4.1.7 adds Faq::isFaqAccessibleForUser() and gates both APIs plus frontend comment fetch.
flaw_origin: The missing-authorization pattern first entered public history on 2015-03-10 in 5611aa5356c9b80cedb8eef16f4d3dea44eb8987, which added phpmyfaq/api.php case getAttachmentsFromFaq that listed filenames/URLs via PMF_Attachment_Factory::fetchByRecordId($recordId) with no parent-FAQ visibility check, while the sibling getFaq case in the same file already called setUser/setGroups and PMF_Faq::getRecord() used queryPermission on faqdata_user/faqdata_group. The same omission was independently copied onto comments on 2016-08-21 in 9b518ea4ca9bd666f1064ea7396e2f6f999b8d4c (case getComments -> getCommentsData). REST v2 renamed the actions (0607413c, 2020-01-02) and 7cb8c2cde1df566fdee27e1ad649c6cb800285aa (2023-07-30) moved the unguarded handlers into AttachmentController::list and CommentController::list; git log -L on those list() bodies stops at that move from api.php. Tag 4.1.6 still calls getCommentsData / fetchByRecordId with no parent check.
ai_marker: absent; BIC author/committer Thorsten Rinne <thorsten@phpmyfaq.de> (2015-03-10); subject/body is only 'Added API endpoint for links to attachments (#982)'; no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, Signed-off-by, Copilot, ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI/tool trailers on the commit object.
evidence: CVE.org/cveawg record CVE-2026-76215 state=PUBLISHED (not withdrawn/rejected); CNA VulnCheck; datePublished 2026-08-19; affected thorsten phpMyFAQ 0 <= version < 4.1.7, 4.1.7 unaffected; CWE-862; references GHSA-jmv9-23mw-mxpq and vulncheck advisory. GHSA-jqpp-mfm2-hfw2 is the GitHub Advisory Database copy of that CVE (withdrawn_at null).

First-party advisory https://github.com/thorsten/phpMyFAQ/security/advisories/GHSA-jmv9-23mw-mxpq (published 2026-08-04): missing parent FAQ authorization exposes comments, commenter PII, and attachment metadata. Lead PoC is unauthenticated GET /api/v3.1/comments/123 returning comment text+email for a group-restricted FAQ whose GET /api/v3.1/faq/1/123 returns 404 {}; additional surfaces are frontend index.php?action=faq (Access denied body, comments still rendered) and GET /api/v3.1/attachments/{recordId} (filename+URL). Vendor page https://www.phpmyfaq.de/security/advisory-2026-08-04 lists the same comments/attachments issue under Moderate and patches it in 4.1.7.

Vulnerable 4.1.6 CommentController::list (phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Controller/Api/CommentController.php:82-93) filters recordId then calls Comments::getCommentsData($recordId, CommentType::FAQ) and json() 200 with no parent visibility check. Vulnerable 4.1.6 AttachmentController::list (same tree, lines 80-102) calls AttachmentFactory::fetchByRecordId and returns filename/url. Routes at 4.1.6 phpmyfaq/src/api-routes.php:61-62 and :96-97 are v{$apiVersion}/attachments/{recordId} and v{$apiVersion}/comments/{recordId}. Contrast: 4.1.6 FaqController.php:163-171 sets current user/groups and 404s when getFaqByIdAndCategoryId yields empty or solution_id===42.

Frontend 4.1.6 phpmyfaq/faq.php:220 always does $comment->getCommentsData((int)$faqId, CommentType::FAQ) even when Faq::getFaq filled faqRecord with solution_id 42 and content=msgAccessDenied (phpmyfaq/src/phpMyFAQ/Faq.php:645-656).

Fix: 10636a21189beb59c08db8a2d300d159406e4b8e (author/committer Thorsten Rinne, 2026-07-26) 'fix: harden child-resource authorization for FAQ records' adds Faq::isFaqAccessibleForUser() mirroring getFaqByIdAndCategoryId permission/active/date filters, returns 404 [] from CommentController and AttachmentController when the parent is not visible, and skips comment fetch/render in faq.php when solution_id===42. git merge-base --is-ancestor 10636a211 4.1.7 YES; not an ancestor of 4.1.6. First tags containing the fix: 4.1.7, 4.1.8. git grep isFaqAccessibleForUser is empty on 4.1.6 and present on 4.1.7 CommentController.php:93, AttachmentController.php:91, Faq.php, and tests.

AI decision is BIC-only: 5611aa5356c9b80cedb8eef16f4d3dea44eb8987 is human maintainer Thorsten Rinne in 2015 with no AI commit-object markers. Comments first-write 9b518ea4 (2016) is the same author and also has no AI trailers. Later 2023-2026 controller refactors were not treated as BICs.
reasoning: CVE-2026-76215 is a real, still-published CWE-862: child resources of a restricted FAQ are readable without the parent FAQ visibility check that already existed on FAQ reads. First-party GHSA-jmv9-23mw-mxpq and the 2026-08-04 vendor advisory confirm the comments API as the lead leak (comment text and commenter email), with the attachments API and frontend comment render as additional surfaces, all patched in 4.1.7. The BIC is the smallest public first-write of that unguarded child-resource-by-recordId API pattern, not the 2023 controller extract. At parent 5d1c692d, api.php had getFaq with setUser/setGroups and getRecord already joined faqdata_user/group through queryPermission, but no attachments action; 5611aa53 added getAttachmentsFromFaq that fetched by recordId only. Comments were not in that commit: 9b518ea4 later added getComments with the same omission (parent 7ca2a6d0 verified absent). Those two handlers were renamed in REST v2 and moved into CommentController/AttachmentController; git log -L on the 4.1.6 list() methods does not reconstruct any finer pre-move member beyond api.php, so the 2015 attachments add remains the surviving first-write of the class. Tag membership: BIC is in 2.9.0 and in 4.1.6; the fix 10636a211 is in 4.1.7 and not in 4.1.6. AI authorship is judged only on the BIC commit object: Thorsten Rinne / thorsten@phpmyfaq.de, 2015, no AI trailers, therefore NOT_AI. PR bodies, later AI-era refactors, and the human fix commit were not used to attribute the introducer.
